summary: Admin API requests intermittently 403 after custom authz policy added to private deployment
description:
Issue summary: After a customer-installed custom authorization policy was deployed to their private control plane, calls to admin endpoints (e.g., /v1/admin/models, /v1/admin/keys) started receiving 403 Forbidden for users who previously had admin access. The problem is intermittent and seems to correlate with requests routed through a new ingress rule that rewrites headers.

Impact: Admin tooling and automation (customer CI that rotates keys and updates model pinning) failed for parts of the fleet. Customer reports ~15% of admin requests are 403; non-admin user APIs are unaffected. This blocks rotation automation and SRE maintenance windows.

Environment: Beacon Analytics private deployment, prod in us-east, private control plane, identity-proxy v1.14.2, custom authz-policy v2 uploaded by customer via Console.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Authenticate as org-admin user via customer IdP (OIDC) and obtain bearer token.
2) Call GET /v1/admin/models with Authorization: Bearer <token> via their load balancer (route A or route B).
3) Observe 403 for some requests; retrying the same call occasionally succeeds.
4) Requests routed through an alternate ingress (route C) succeed consistently.

Logs / evidence:
- Sample 403 response (truncated): {
  "status": 403,
  "message": "forbidden: insufficient roles"
}
- Identity-proxy logs show: "policy_evaluate: matched policy 'deny_legacy_admin' precedence=50" for 403 requests.
- Successful request entries show "policy_evaluate: no deny rule matched; allowed by default".
- Ingress access logs correlate failing requests to LB backend instance id b-7f3a that applies an X-Route header.

Customer notes: They installed a packaged policy intended to block legacy maintenance endpoints in staging but the same policy was inadvertently applied in prod. The policy uses header matching and a precedence field; order of evaluation appears to cause the deny rule to capture legitimate admin requests when the ingress rewrites a header used in the rule.

Requested outcome: Help identify why policy is matching admin requests, provide a short-term mitigation (policy change or routing tweak) and guidance on longer-term safe policy rollout practices.
investigation_notes: 03/10 - Support triage: Confirmed 403s only for admin endpoints; not a token expiry or IdP claim issue per initial token inspection.

03/10 - Identity team: Pulled policy bundle the customer uploaded; found 'deny_legacy_admin' with header match condition 'X-Api-Route =~ /legacy/'. Policy precedence=50 (higher numbers evaluated earlier).

03/11 - Ingress team: Verified that LB route A rewrites path and sets X-Api-Route="legacy-admin" for internal routing. Route C does not set this header. This explains why some requests match deny rule only when routed through A.
03/11 - Reproduced: Deployed a local policy with same match and saw deterministic denies when X-Api-Route header present. When header removed, policy not matched and request allowed.

03/12 - Hypothesis: Policy precedence ordering in identity-proxy evaluates deny_legacy_admin before tenant-scoped allow rules; because deny matches on header only, it short-circuits allow by higher-precedence deny rule. Also possible misconfiguration: customer intended the policy to run in staging only but scope metadata contained 'prod' by mistake.

03/12 - Temporary mitigation tested: Added an explicit allow rule for tenant-admins with higher precedence (70) in a test bundle; admin requests succeed even when header present. This suggests precedence change will mitigate.

03/12 - Risk assessment: Patching precedence in customer-managed policy is lower-risk than changing LB header rewrite; however customer prefers a guidance-first approach and an option to rollback policy via Console.

resolution:
Mitigation applied: In customer's staging replica we added a tenant-scoped 'allow_admins' policy with precedence=70 which overrides the deny rule. Customer agreed to a phased remediation: 1) Rollback the uploaded deny_legacy_admin policy in prod via Console (actioned by customer ops). 2) Add an explicit tenant-admin allow rule in the policy bundle with precedence > deny if customer intends to keep deny rule. 3) Long-term: add a Console validation step to warn when policies include header-based matches that overlap with LB rewrites and provide a safe rollout toggle.

Follow-ups: Engineering to prepare a small identity-proxy update that adds a policy-preview tool (INT ticket) and a Confluence runbook for customers documenting safe policy scope and precedence examples. Customer reports immediate restoration of admin automation after rollback. Marking as monitoring; will close once customer confirms stable for 48 hours.
next_steps: Customer to rollback deny_legacy_admin policy in prod (in progress by Beacon Ops).
Support to validate admin endpoints for 48 hours post-rollback and monitor 403 rate (Support will check daily dashboards).
Identity Eng to open INT ticket for policy-preview feature and add Console rollout warning (INT-512).
Create a short runbook for customers: recommended precedence ranges, recommended header naming to avoid collisions with LB rewrites, and a rollback checklist.
If customer wants to keep deny rule: recommend explicit tenant-admin allow with precedence > deny and update sample policy templates.
